day_shape: 55 items: Iran International reports Mojtaba Khamenei sent Rezaei to Moscow seeking S-400s, IRGC claims 16th MQ-1 downed over Qeshm, tanker explosion off Khasab, Araghchi phones Iraqi and Emirati counterparts; nothing from UK Parliament, OFAC or IAEA.

threads.label: Iran-Russia outreach and energy lifeline
threads.summary: Iran International, citing The Telegraph, reported Mojtaba Khamenei sent security chief Mohsen Rezaei to Moscow with a personal letter to Putin requesting S-400 air defence systems. Deputy SNSC Secretary Ali Bagheri confirmed a roughly three-hour Putin meeting delivering the leader's message, while a separate Iran International piece said gas-rich Iran is seeking Russian supplies before winter.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz incidents and drone claims
threads.summary: Defa Press reported an explosion on a tanker near Khasab, Oman, citing UKMTO, and the IRGC claimed interception of a 16th US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island. The FT, via Iran International, reported Iran-linked ships looped and went dark over Gulf of Oman undersea cables after Tehran's threats to regional digital infrastructure.

threads.label: Iran regional diplomacy after war
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi held phone calls with Iraqi counterpart Fouad Hussein and UAE's Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed on regional stability, per Defa Press. Ali Bagheri said Iran will no longer accept US "paper commitments" and demands practical steps before any new diplomatic phase.

threads.label: US posture and possible renewed Iran strike
threads.summary: Ynet, via Iran International, reported an Israeli strike on Iran remains possible though no major US buildup is detected; Trump told reporters Iran was largely destroyed and would take over two decades to rebuild. The Jerusalem Post reported Trump administration contacts with Tehran over deporting ICE-detained asylum seekers during the war.

threads.label: Tehran pressure on diaspora and Europe
threads.summary: Belgium's defence minister said Tehran warned of dire consequences if Reza Pahlavi were allowed to speak in Brussels, and the event proceeded anyway, per Iran International. IRIB warned "expatriate traitors" face arrest and asset confiscation, while an Iran International investigation detailed Tehran-linked financing of ostensibly independent foreign media.

events.title_en: Mansour Anwari, author of the longest novel of sacred defence, has passed away
events.summary_en: Mansour Anwari, author of the 12-volume series 'War Road', one of the longest novels of war and revolution, who spent more than 30 years of his life writing the history of the revolution and sacred defence, has passed away. The novel 'War Road' by Mansour Anwari is among the major works of Iranian fictional literature that, with a historical perspective, narrates the fate of people and political and social developments of the country in the context of war and historical crises. This series, passing through several important periods of contemporary history, attempts to depict the impact of war on people's lives, the fate of the land, and social developments in Iran in narrative form.

events.title_en: Nujaba Movement: Popular Mobilisation is the backbone of Iraq
events.summary_en: The Nujaba Movement described the Popular Mobilisation as the backbone of Iraq and the safety valve of the country, emphasising the importance of preserving it as a factor to neutralise any conspiracy by enemies against the country. The Nujaba Movement's statement stressed that the Popular Mobilisation is the beating heart of Iraq and the true manifestation of belief in resistance. The statement added that the Popular Mobilisation is a thorn in the eye of dependent (mercenary) currents. The statement said that changes that lead to the fragmentation and weakening of the Popular Mobilisation should not be endorsed. The Nujaba Movement stressed that standing against this conspiracy is repaying the debt to the pure blood of Abu Mahdi.
